problem: Existing embodied simulators focus on indoor/household or tabletop tasks; urban simulators (CARLA, AirSim, MetaUrban) either lack procedural generation, photorealism, non-vehicle agents, or realistic pedestrian/traffic dynamics, and no benchmark jointly tests multimodal instruction following, safe navigation among people/traffic and multi-robot communication at city scale.
motivation: Real-world outdoor robotics needs 3D grounding in large environments, safe navigation with pedestrians and traffic, long-range memory and multi-agent collaboration. A scalable, photorealistic, dynamic urban simulator would allow both training data generation and systematic evaluation of foundation models for these capacities.
key_idea: Build an Unreal Engine 5 platform that procedurally generates photorealistic, dynamic city-scale environments with pedestrians, traffic, vehicles and robots, and use it to create a multimodal urban navigation benchmark (SimWorld-MMNav) plus a two-robot communication/search benchmark (SimWorld-MRS) and a 20K-step training set.
insight: Current VLMs, including strong proprietary and reasoning models, almost never complete long multi-subtask urban navigation (SR 0-8%), failing mainly at intersection detection, distance estimation, embodied/active perception, and matching landmarks across viewpoints (failure-mode table). Fine-tuning a 7B VLM on only 20K oracle steps with auxiliary supervision (distance, orientation, action plan) raises subtask SR from 16.86 to 52.45, showing simulator-generated data helps, while the ablation shows explicit ReAct reasoning and segmentation give the largest gains for zero-shot GPT-4o (34.38 vs 32.21/31.90), and depth adds nothing.
method: Procedural city generation: four stages (road network via priority-queue tree growth with intersection checks, collision-aware building placement with greedy gap filling, street elements like trees/cones/benches/parked cars, and traffic elements) from minimal specifications.

Embodied agents and asynchronous control: humans (26 actions), vehicles (continuous acceleration/brake/steer) and robots (scooter, quadruped) controlled asynchronously through a centralized buffer; RGB, depth, segmentation observations plus GT descriptions and 3D boxes; Python/Gym API over UnrealCV.

Background traffic system: city-wide waypoint graph (road waypoints every 17 m, intersection waypoints) that pedestrians and vehicles follow, PID-based vehicle control, traffic lights (proceed only if green with >15s remaining), probabilistic routing.

SimWorld-MMNav benchmark: A*-derived paths decomposed into chained subtasks (Orientation Alignment, Move Along the Road, Turn at Intersection, Reach Destination), each with a language instruction plus a visual hint image; easy (no obstacles) and hard (static obstacles, pedestrians, vehicles, traffic lights) sets; metrics SR, Subtask SR, Distance Progress, collisions, red-light violations.

SimWorld-20K and fine-tuned baseline: 200 oracle A* trajectories on 100 training maps (about 20K steps, 66% of building types), Qwen2.5-VL-7B LoRA fine-tuned to predict remaining distance, expected orientation, remaining action plan, then next action.

Zero-shot/hybrid/RL baselines: perception module (describes observation vs. visual hint) plus text-only ReAct action module with memory summary; HybridGPT (GPT-4o high-level + A* low-level); VLA-RL (DeBERTa-v3 + DINOv2, BC then PPO).

SimWorld-MRS benchmark: main robot has map and 20+ landmark images, follower does not; follower describes its view, main robot localizes it by tournament-style VLM retrieval, then oracle A* planning or RoCo-style joint rendezvous planning with natural-language path instructions.

setting.backbone: Zero-shot VLMs with ReAct (GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, GPT-o3, GPT-o3-pro, Qwen2.5-VL 7B/72B, Gemma 3 27B, InternVL 3 78B); Qwen2.5-VL-7B (LoRA fine-tuned); VLA-RL (DeBERTa-v3 + DINOv2, trained with BC+PPO); HybridGPT
setting.training_data: SimWorld-20K: 200 A* oracle trajectories, ~20K steps, 100 procedurally generated training maps (2 km2 each); zero-shot models use none
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + segmentation (+ depth, excluded in zero-shot baselines) + compass orientation + language instruction + visual hint image
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward/backward/left/right (5 m), turn left/right 90°, stay, 'evaluate' (subtask complete); in MRS also send natural-language messages and check_task_complete
setting.privileged: MMNav: none for VLMs (GT compass given, GT segmentation used); HybridGPT and MRS oracle/RoCo use A* with GT city map, main robot has full map and landmark memory

numbers_note: The text of the MRS results paragraph quotes GPT-4o oracle CSR 52% and progress 68.44%, which conflicts with Table 5 (65.00/76.90); table values used. Ablation (Table 6) is on a 50-task subset. Benchmarks are new and not in the canonical list. HM MMNav split is the paper's own test tasks.
results: All non-reasoning zero-shot VLMs get 0% SR on MMNav easy; best zero-shot is GPT-o3-pro at 8.3% SR, while fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-7B gets 4.0% SR but the best Subtask SR (52.45) and Distance Progress (53.63), beating GPT-o3-pro (46.35/39.46). VLA-RL (0/28.37/22.79) and HybridGPT (0/32.53/27.24) do not beat zero-shot VLMs. In MRS, GPT-4o with an oracle planner reaches 65.00% CSR but RoCo drops to 33.33% and Qwen2.5-VL-72B RoCo to 11.11%.
limitations: Outdoor only with limited human action space; pedestrian behaviour is rule-based; no indoor scenes.

Small evaluation sets (about 100 tasks per benchmark, low absolute SR), fine-tuning only on oracle trajectories so no error recovery, hard-set results only for 3 models, and only a few baselines on MRS.
Zero-shot baselines exclude depth and use a hand-designed perceive/ReAct pipeline, so failures may partially reflect pipeline design; no real-robot validation.
